newsitem.title: USA: High moisture content slows Illinois corn harvest.
newsitem.headline: High moisture content slows Illinois corn harvest.

text.p: High moisture content in corn and late soybean maturity slowed harvest progress in the week ended Sunday, Illinois' Agricultural Statistics Service said in its weekly crop update.
Corn was 22 percent harvested, lagging the five-year average of 42 percent. Soybeans were 34 percent harvested, below the average of 73 percent.
Corn was 89 percent mature as of Sunday, behind the 98 percent five-year average. Ninety percent of the soybean plants were dropping leaves, lagging average of 98 percent, the report said.
Slow soybean harvest progress was also delaying winter wheat seeding, the report said. Soft red winter wheat was 29 percent planted as of Sunday, behind the 49 percent five-year average.
Six percent of the crop had emerged, against 12 percent average.
Sorghum was six percent harvested, compared with 33 percent for the five-year average. The crop was 70 percent mature, also behind the five-year average of 87 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 62 percent adequate, 33 percent short and four percent very short.
